entities.summary: Saadi Shirazi (1210-1291) was an Iranian Sufi poet who played a pivotal role in shaping the spiritual and literary landscape of the Middle East during the 13th century. Born in Baghdad, Iraq, Saadi was influenced by the works of Rumi and Hafez, and his own writings, including the famous poem 'Gulistan', reflected a deep understanding of Islamic mysticism and social commentary. As a prominent figure in the Sufi movement, Saadi's poetry and teachings attracted a devoted following among scholars and mystics, and his legacy continues to be celebrated in Iran and beyond. Despite the destruction of many of his manuscripts during the Mongol invasions, Saadi's works have endured, and his poetry remains a testament to the power of Sufi mysticism to inspire and transform lives. The city of Shiraz, where Saadi lived and died, remains a sacred place for Sufi pilgrims and scholars, who come to pay homage to the poet's memory and to reflect on the timeless wisdom of his writings.
